decisions.reason: As a newly launched niche reusable crate, it should be kept because after only one year its market potential is still uncertain and the cost of leaving it in the portfolio is likely modest for a large packaging producer.

Its dedicated product page suggests meaningful strategic interest or early customer relevance, so the firm would keep the option open while learning more about demand for foldable logistics containers.
A stackable plastic crate fits the firm’s core reusable transport offering, and with so little time elapsed since launch there is not yet enough evidence to justify abandonment.
A medium-duty rackable pallet is close to the company’s established pallet business, so retaining it is a low-cost way to preserve upside until customer adoption becomes clearer.
Its own webpage indicates a stronger commercial commitment, and spill-retention applications can provide differentiated value, making it sensible to continue the product while uncertainty resolves.

Because it received dedicated website presentation and extends the firm’s core pallet line with a functional improvement, management would likely keep it on the market to gather more evidence before deciding on further commitment.
